name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project with customized Dockerfile and .dockerfile files.

Containerize only the changes required to run the specified ASP.NET (.NET Framework, not .NET Core) project in a Windows Docker container. Honor all settings below; unspecified settings use defaults.

Settings:
- Project: `[ProjectName (provide path to .csproj file)]`
- Windows Server SKU: `[Windows Server Core (Default) or Windows Server Full]`; version: `[2016, 2019, or 2022]`
- Custom build/run base images: `[Specify base image to use for build/run stage (Default None)]`
- Exposed primary/additional ports: `[e.g., 80]` / `[List any additional ports, or "None"]`
- Container user: `[User account, or default to "ContainerUser"]`
- IIS settings: `[List any specific IIS settings, or "None"]`
- Custom steps before/after image build: `[List any specific build steps, or "None"]`
- GAC assemblies, MSIs, COM components: `[Names/versions, or "None"]`
- Registry keys/values: `[Registry paths and values, or "None"]`
- Environment variables: `[Variable names and values, or "Use defaults"]`
- Windows roles/features: `[Role/feature names, or "None"]`
- Files/directories to copy: `[Paths relative to project root, or "None"]`; target: `[Container paths, or "Not applicable"]`
- Exclusions: `[Paths to exclude, or "None"]`
- Additional `.dockerignore` patterns: `[List any additional patterns, or "None"]`
- Health check URL and interval/timeout: `[Health check URL path, or "None"]` / `[Interval and timeout values, or "Use defaults"]`
- Other requirements and known issues: `[Specific requirements, or "None"]` / `[Describe any known issues, or "None"]`

✅ App configuration modification to use config builders for environment-based app settings and connection strings; Dockerfile with multi-stage build/publish; Windows compatibility; dependency handling (GAC, MSIs, COM).
❌ No infrastructure setup (assumed to be handled separately)
❌ No code changes beyond those required for containerization

Procedure:
1. Review settings.
2. Create `progress.md` to track changes with check marks.
3. Determine .NET Framework version from the `.csproj` `TargetFrameworkVersion`.
4. Select the Windows Server image for detected .NET Framework version, specified SKU (Core or Full), and version (2016, 2019, or 2022). Tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
5. Required NuGet package: `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If they are not installed, the user must install them manually. If they are not installed, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console.
6. Modify `web.config` to read app settings and connection strings from environment variables. Add configBuilders in configSections and root; configure EnvironmentConfigBuilder for both:
`<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />`
`<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />`
`<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">` (retain existing settings)
`<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">` (retain existing strings)
7. Create `LogMonitorConfig.json` in the Dockerfile folder by copying the reference content below. The file's contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless instructions in containerization settings specify otherwise. Do not change EventLog issue logging level to `Information`; it causes unnecessary noise.
8. Create a root `Dockerfile` with multiple stages. Build stage uses Windows Server Core and `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk` unless a custom build image is specified. Copy sln, csproj, and packages.config first; copy `NuGet.config` if present and configure private feeds; restore NuGet packages; copy remaining source; use MSBuild to build/publish to `C:\publish`. Final stage uses selected Windows Server image and `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/aspnet` unless a custom run image is specified. Copy `LogMonitorConfig.json` into the container (e.g., `C:\LogMonitor`), download LogMonitor.exe from https://github.com/microsoft/windows-container-tools/releases/download/v2.1.1/LogMonitor.exe, set working directory to `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`, copy `C:\publish` output, and run LogMonitor.exe with ServiceMonitor.exe to monitor IIS:
`ENTRYPOINT [ "C:\\LogMonitor\\LogMonitor.exe", "C:\\ServiceMonitor.exe", "w3svc" ]`
Honor SKU/version, user, GAC, COM, roles/features, and file-copy settings. Model after the supplied example, customized to the project. **IMPORTANT:** Use a Windows Server Core base image unless the user has **specifically requested** a full Windows Server image in the settings file
9. Create root `.dockerignore`. The `.dockerignore` file **MUST** include at least the following elements as well as additional patterns as specified in the containerization settings: all additional specified patterns.
10. If a health check endpoint is provided, add `HEALTHCHECK` to Dockerfile.
11. Add `<None Include="Dockerfile" />` to the project file.
12. Mark completed tasks `[ ]` → `[✓]`; continue until all tasks are complete and Docker build succeeds.
13. Confirm Docker build succeeds once the Dockerfile is completed. Use the following command to build the Docker image:
`docker build -t aspnet-app:latest .`
If the build fails, review errors and adjust Dockerfile or project configuration. Report success/failure.
Maintain `progress.md` with:
[ ] .NET Framework version detection (version: ___)
[ ] Windows Server SKU selection (SKU: ___)
[ ] Windows Server version selection (Version: ___)
[ ] Web.config modifications for configuration builders
[ ] NuGet package source configuration (if applicable)
[ ] Copy LogMonitorConfig.json and adjust if required by settings
[ ] .dockerignore file creation
[ ] Build stage created with SDK image
[ ] sln, csproj, packages.config, and (if applicable) N
